record.paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
record.original_question: For feedback-controlled flashing ratchets, existing bounds relate flux improvement and power-output improvement to information used by the controller per actuation. How can those bounds be reformulated in terms of the total non-redundant information acquired per unit time, so that the ratchet bounds can be related to the entropy-reduction and thermodynamic framework for general feedback-controlled systems?

evidence.quote: relations between the information I (about the system) gathered by the controller per step and the performance have been recently obtained
These relation were stated in terms of the information per actuation.
total amount of information per unit time (i.e., only computing non-redundant information per unit time) is still an open question

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a flashing Brownian ratchet operating under feedback control: a single (or collective) Brownian particle moves in one dimension subject to thermal noise at temperature T, and a controller can switch on or off an asymmetric periodic potential V(x) based on measurements of the particle's state. Let the controller perform actuations (switching decisions) at discrete times, and at each actuation let I_step denote the Shannon mutual information between the measurement outcome used and the system state. Known bounds express the improvement in the steady-state particle flux ⟨ẋ⟩ and in the extractable power output P (against an opposing load) over the open-loop (uncontrolled) ratchet as functions of I_step, the information used per actuation.

Because successive measurements may share information, I_step overcounts when integrated over time. Define the total non-redundant information rate Ṙ acquired by the controller as the asymptotic rate

  Ṙ = lim_{t→∞} (1/t) · I(X_{[0,t]} ; Y_{[0,t]}),

where X_{[0,t]} is the trajectory of the system, Y_{[0,t]} is the sequence of measurement outcomes used by the controller on [0,t], and I(·;·) is the Shannon mutual information; equivalently, Ṙ may be taken as the transfer entropy rate from the system to the controller. This quantity Ṙ is the appropriate information input rate that enters the generalized second law and entropy-reduction (Sagawa–Ueda type) bounds for feedback-controlled thermodynamic systems.

Problem: Reformulate the existing upper bounds on the flux improvement ⟨ẋ⟩_fb − ⟨ẋ⟩_open and on the power-output improvement P_fb − P_open of the feedback-controlled flashing ratchet as explicit bounds in terms of the non-redundant information rate Ṙ (rather than in terms of the per-actuation information I_step), thereby relating these ratchet performance bounds directly to the entropy-reduction/second-law framework for general feedback-controlled systems.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature establishes per-actuation information bounds on flux and power for feedback flashing ratchets, and a separate body of work develops entropy-reduction/second-law bounds using information rates for general feedback systems. Recent Markovian descriptions of feedback flashing ratchets have appeared, but no source clearly reformulates the ratchet bounds in terms of non-redundant information per unit time. Status appears unresolved based on available search results.

status_evidence.title: Information and flux in a feedback controlled Brownian ratchet
status_evidence.snippet: flux in the feedback case has an upper bound proportional to the square-root of the information
status_evidence.claim: Existing bounds are stated in terms of information per actuation.

status_evidence.title: Markovian description of a wide class of feedback-controlled systems: application to the feedback flashing ratchet
status_evidence.snippet: Markovian description of feedback-controlled systems applied to flashing ratchet
status_evidence.claim: Recent work develops a Markovian framework but does not explicitly close the reformulation in terms of non-redundant information rate.

status_evidence.title: Information and maximum power in a feedback controlled Brownian ratchet
status_evidence.snippet: information and maximum power in feedback controlled Brownian ratchet
status_evidence.claim: Power-output bounds are formulated per actuation rather than per unit time.
